marks.gloss_en: דתניא: תפלין ומזוזות אין נכתבין אלא אשורית, ורבותינו התירו יוונית (kind svara: no SupportKind names דתניא; the source is the reading the stam goes on to emend)
כי תניא ההיא בשאר ספרים ורבי יהודה היא -- the baraita speaks of the other books and is R' Yehuda's (= p_ashi_shear_sefarim, p_ashi_ryehuda_hi)
Rav Ashi: that baraita is taught of the other books [of scripture]
ותניא, אמר רבי יהודה: אף כשהתירו רבותינו יוונית — לא התירו אלא בספר תורה (kind svara: no SupportKind names ותניא)
the stam's second emendation: our Rabbis permitted them [scrolls] to be written only in Greek
דתניא: מעשה בתלמי המלך... -- the maaseh of the seventy-two elders (kind svara: no SupportKind names דתניא)
R' Yehuda: and [it was permitted] because of the maaseh of King Ptolemy
כאן במגילה, כאן בספרים -- the baraita speaks of the Megilla (= p_kan_bimegillah; its difficulty answered at 9a.7)
מאי תרגום שכתבו מקרא איכא? -- what targum written as scripture is there in the Megilla?
rather, no difficulty: here [the baraita] the Megilla, there [the mishna] scrolls

במאי אוקימתא להא? בגופן שלהן -- מאי איריא מקרא שכתבו תרגום ותרגום שכתבו מקרא? אפילו מקרא שכתבו מקרא ותרגום שכתבו תרגום נמי, דהא קתני: עד שיכתבנו אשורית על הספר בדיו! -- in their script even scripture written as scripture would be excluded, so why does the baraita single out the crossings?
אי רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, הא איכא יוונית! -- RSBG permits Greek, but the baraita admits only Ashurit
rather, no difficulty: here [the mishna] scrolls, there [the baraita] tefillin and mezuzot

מאי תרגום שכתבו מקרא איכא? בשלמא תורה — איכא יגר שהדותא, אלא הכא מאי תרגום איכא? -- the Torah contains targum (Gen 31:47), but what targum is there in tefillin and mezuzot for the baraita's 'targum written as scripture'?
tefillin and mezuzot -- what is the reason? because it is written of them 'and they shall be' (Deut 6:6): as they are, so shall they be
ונשמע פתגם המלך (Est 1:20) (= p_pitgam_targum)
וכל הנשים יתנו יקר לבעליהן (Est 1:20) (= p_yekar_targum)
Rav Pappa: 'and the king's decree (pitgam) shall be heard' (Est 1:20) -- [the Megilla does contain targum]
והכתיב והיו! -- tefillin and mezuzot must be as they are written, so 'our Rabbis' cannot have permitted Greek for them
התירו?! מכלל דתנא קמא אסר! -- 'permitted' implies the first clause forbade Greek, yet it says scrolls are written in any language
the stam's first emendation: scrolls are written in any language, and our Rabbis permitted Greek
Rava: no difficulty -- the mishna speaks of [another language] in our script, the baraita of [another language] in their script
rather, no difficulty: this [the mishna] is the Rabbis, that [the baraita] is RSBG
they wrote for him: 'God created in the beginning' (for Gen 1:1, Steinsaltz)
'and He finished on the sixth day and rested on the seventh day' (for Gen 2:2, Steinsaltz)
'come, let me go down and confound their language there' (for Gen 11:7, Steinsaltz)
'for in their anger they slew an ox and in their will uprooted a trough' (for Gen 49:6, Steinsaltz)
'and the dwelling of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt and in other lands was four hundred years' (for Ex 12:40, Steinsaltz)
